headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Superset’s allowlisted egress if paired workflows move sensitive content into its API; prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks are otherwise limited by LlamaFactory’s non-runnable, no-I/O profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Superset output by default. Superset does expose a Superset API and allowlisted egress, so a manual or orchestrated bridge could still carry attacker-controlled text. The pathway is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Superset output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator forwards Superset API responses into LlamaFactory without sanitization, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste bridging between the two tools.
Add a prompt sanitizer before any Superset-to-LlamaFactory handoff.
Require human review of any API payload before reuse.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from Superset text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LlamaFactory is non-runnable and shows no filesystem or network egress, so it is not the leakage source. Superset has allowlisted network egress and a Superset API, so if shared data enters Superset workflows, it can leave the local boundary through its backend integrations. The pair can therefore leak data in default-style analytics workflows, though the profiles do not show sensitive classes touched.
conditions: IF sensitive records are loaded into Superset dashboards or queries, they may be transmitted via allowlisted egress.
IF LlamaFactory-generated text is pasted into Superset notes or SQL, it can be exposed through Superset API-backed workflows.
mitigations: Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive tables.
Turn off any unnecessary Superset connectors or exports.
Keep LlamaFactory outputs out of shared dashboards.
Review outbound allowlist entries in Superset.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Superset egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it has no mutable overlap with Superset beyond API-level interaction. Superset’s allowlisted egress does not create a write-write conflict with LlamaFactory. No shared mutable resource is evidenced in either profile.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access, conflict risk could emerge.
IF both agents are later deployed against the same mutable workspace, reassess.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only as profiled.
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Do not grant Superset write access to the same repo or directory.
Document any future shared resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory can generate model outputs, and Superset can consume API-driven inputs and present them in analytics workflows. If Superset treats LlamaFactory output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream actions. The profiles do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Superset ingests LlamaFactory output as facts without validation, incorrect content can propagate.
IF a downstream workflow acts on Superset-rendered results, the cascade extends beyond reporting.
mitigations: Require source verification before Superset ingestion.
Label LlamaFactory output as untrusted in dashboards.
Add a review step for any AI-generated fields.
Separate generated text from operational metrics.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on AI-derived inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile shows PHI, EU-only residency, or special certifications, so a concrete compliance breach is not evidenced. The only relevant compliance surface is Superset’s API and allowlisted egress, while LlamaFactory has no data classes touched. This is a low-risk gap because future residency or retention mismatches would depend on deployment choices not shown here.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through Superset, residency and retention controls must be rechecked.
IF LlamaFactory is used to process protected data, the deployment policy must define handling rules.
mitigations: Confirm whether any regulated data is in scope.
Review Superset retention settings.
Document data residency for any outbound connectors.
Keep protected data out of both tools until policy is set.
